uncited: Computes the probability density function (PDF) value of a 2D Gaussian distribution at a specific 2D point, given its mean vector and covariance matrix.
It serves as the core evaluation primitive for determining the contribution of a projected 3D Gaussian splat to a pixel in Gaussian Splatting rendering.
It differs from its sibling [Gaussian Interpolation](2347-gaussian-interpolation.md) by providing a direct analytical evaluation of the density rather than interpolating values between grid points.
**Compute Mean Difference:** Calculate the vector from the Gaussian mean to the evaluation point.
**Compute Determinant:** Calculate the determinant of the covariance matrix.
**Compute Inverse Covariance:** Calculate the inverse of the $2 \times 2$ covariance matrix analytically.
**Compute Quadratic Form:** Calculate the Mahalanobis distance squared (quadratic form).
**Return PDF:** Compute the final normalized probability density.
- No tunable parameters; this is a deterministic mathematical evaluation.
- **Singular Covariance:** If $\det(\Sigma) = 0$, the inverse is undefined.
For very large covariances, the exponent may underflow to 0.
Standard IEEE 754 floating-point behavior applies.
The code assumes $\Sigma_{01} = \Sigma_{10}$.
If the input matrix is not symmetric, the result may be incorrect.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per evaluation.
Involves a fixed number of arithmetic operations (additions, multiplications, square root, exponential).
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ auxiliary memory.
No approximation errors from grid sampling.
Does not handle occlusion or depth sorting (those are handled by the rasterization pipeline).
- **When to use:** When evaluating the contribution of a single Gaussian splat to a specific pixel coordinate.

- **When not to use:** When gradients are needed (use [Gradient of 2D Gaussian PDF (Conic)](3472-gradient-of-2d-gaussian-pdf-conic.md)) or when computing alpha compositing over multiple splats (use [Single Point Alpha Forward](3478-single-point-alpha-forward.md) or the full rasterizer).
It is a fundamental component of the EWA (Elliptical Weighted Average) splatting technique used to project 3D Gaussians onto the 2D image plane.
The method relies on the standard definition of the multivariate Gaussian distribution.
